body:
## Purpose

The S3 client every later slice calls through. Named explicitly because it was implicit in the
original slicing and therefore in nobody's brief.

## Scope

- `aws-sdk-s3` wiring against an arbitrary `--endpoint`: path-style addressing, region and service
  scope, static credentials, no anonymous path.
- SigV4 header auth over plain HTTP (the gateway's public TLS is blocked pending a
  dependency/license decision — `crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:50-57`).
- Response handling: map S3 XML error bodies onto typed errors carrying status, `Code`, and
  `x-amz-request-id`, so every later assertion can name what it expected and what it got.
- Streaming both ways — a PUT is chunked as it is generated and a GET read incrementally, so no
  object is ever fully resident. The whole point is objects larger than memory.

## Definition of done

- One object round-trips PUT → GET → DELETE against a loopback `wyrd s3`.
- An error response surfaces its status, `Code` and request id rather than a stringified blob.
- A 5 GiB payload streams without the process resident set tracking object size.

Depends on #740
Part of #735. Plan of record: proposal 0017.

comments.body:
## Two blockers the plan review found

### 1. `aws-sdk-s3` moves from dev-dependency into a shipped artifact — a NEEDS-HUMAN license item

It is currently dev-only: `crates/server/Cargo.toml:120-129`, noted there as not compiled into the production binary. This slice makes it a **normal** dependency of a shipped workspace member, which brings roughly a hundred crates inside `deny.toml`'s frame — whose own header says it "guards the default feature graph — the artifact we ship".

`docs/INTEGRATION.md` §4 names "any new dependency or license (the ADR-0003 three-test audit + `deny.toml` allowlist)" a human-only item. So this needs the audit **before** the crate lands, not after CI goes red.

Related and immediate: **#726** is already open — "CI red on every PR: cargo-deny advisory wall trips RUSTSEC-2026-0253 (lru, via aws-sdk-s3 dev-dependency)". It appears waived on `main` (commit `1d75927` mirrors the waiver into `deny-all-features.toml`), but a waiver scoped to a dev-dependency may not cover the same crate as a shipped one. Confirm before starting.

### 2. Scope says "SigV4 over plain HTTP" — which is not how a real endpoint is deployed

Proposal 0017 §10 and blueprint §B.1 make the S3 port the only public exposure, behind an operator's own TLS terminator. Nothing in this slice or any other adds a TLS client, and adding one meets the wall the gateway already sits behind: a rustls crypto provider outside the `deny.toml` allowlist, flagged NEEDS-HUMAN at `crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:50-57`.

As scoped, the tool validates only the configuration operators are told not to run — and the 7-day Alpha evidence artifact would be produced over plain HTTP with static credentials. That is now stated in the proposal's *Dependencies* rather than left implicit, but it is a real limit on what the gating run licenses.

### Sizing

Still oversized against the calibrated backstop: SDK wiring + SigV4 + typed error mapping + bidirectional streaming + a 5 GiB memory property, and the last of those is blocked on #635 (see #744, #761). Consider splitting the streaming/large-object leg out.

Refs #735, #726, proposal 0017 §Dependencies.
